briefing.opening: Good morning. We will now begin the climate briefing for August 14, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Global Climate Crisis Warning: Extreme Weather Events and Deepening Impacts
sections.content: Direct impacts of extreme weather events are spreading domestically, with heatwaves and tropical nights doubling in the Gyeongbuk region, and work stoppages occurring due to heatwaves [1, 6]. Internationally, climate change has been confirmed to have widespread effects on global ecosystems and industries, including difficulties for Italy's cheese banks, a water crisis in Puerto Rico, severe snow drought in the Western U.S., and accelerated mercury release in Antarctica [24, 25, 26, 28]. Notably, in the UK, droughts and large-scale wildfires swept across the country, prompting the Prime Minister to emphasize the need to 'confront climate change' [31, 44, 46, 50], while flood plans in the Midlands clearly demonstrate rising costs due to climate change [29]. This situation suggests an urgency, as expressed by the concern of elderly residents in the Delta region that 'later is too late' [33], and research has also shown that climate change exacerbates social vulnerabilities, such as increasing child marriage [41].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Climate Response Efforts: Policy, Technology, and Investment in Future Generations
sections.content: The institutional foundation for domestic climate policy is being strengthened, with the National Assembly's Special Committee on Climate concluding 17 months of activity by passing the Carbon Neutrality Framework Act and the Climate Crisis Adaptation Act [10]. The government is participating in international climate action by approving implementation agreements under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement [5], and Korea University hosted a mock UNFCCC conference to foster climate leadership among future generations [3]. Furthermore, local communities and educational institutions are actively engaged in climate adaptation and carbon neutrality efforts, such as Goheung County proactively securing agricultural water to minimize drought damage [8], and Gwangmyeong City youth visiting advanced carbon-neutral cities in Germany to learn for the future [9, 11, 13].

sections.title: 🌱 Energy Transition and the AI Era: Seeking New Challenges and Solutions
sections.content: The advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology has led to a surge in electricity demand and raised issues regarding the variability of renewable energy, further highlighting the complexity of energy transition [14]. Against this backdrop, the Korean Prime Minister met with Bill Gates to discuss energy mix solutions, including renewable energy and Small Modular Reactors (SMRs), seeking AI power solutions [15, 18, 20]. Private investment is also continuing, with Naver acquiring stakes in wind power companies to secure power for its AI data centers [17]. Meanwhile, Korea South-East Power (KOEN) announced plans to build a carbon-free power ecosystem linking solar, green hydrogen, and hydrogen power for the first time in Korea, presenting innovative alternatives [16]. In India, the world's largest single-site Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) was completed, setting a new standard in the renewable energy storage competition [19]. However, many challenges remain in the energy transition process, as exemplified by Posco International, where LNG and gas field projects still form the main basis of their performance [12], and the World Resources Institute (WRI) warns that global water policies are off track [4].

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Climate Responsibility: Loss and Damage, Adaptation, and Policy Debates
sections.content: Nepal's new question regarding 'loss and damage' – whether climate disasters are due to climate change – urges the international community to engage in deep discussions on climate responsibility and compensation [2]. Amidst this, research on how Baja California fishermen adapt to climate change [39] and advice provided by UC experts on climate change to Cincinnati [23] emphasize the importance of practical adaptation efforts at the local level. However, in the UK, environmental groups are urging Andy Burnham to break his silence on the climate crisis [22], and Burnham is criticized for his electric vehicle and North Sea policies [40, 45], indicating active debates and criticisms surrounding climate policy. Furthermore, China's announcement of its 15th Five-Year Plan for coal has significant implications for global climate action [34, 51], and as noted by the observation that extreme weather events are becoming a battleground in culture wars [30], climate change is expanding beyond a simple environmental issue into a complex social and political problem.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted various domestic and international efforts to address the deepening global climate crisis, alongside ongoing discussions and challenges regarding energy transition and climate responsibility. This concludes today's climate briefing.
